s1.syndrome_frame: a chronic skin condition characterized by asymptomatic red to brown macules and papules with a symmetric distribution on the trunk and extremities
salient_findings: red to brown macules and papules on trunk and extremities
elevated tryptase and vitamin B12 levels
key_facts: male patient in his 20s
12-month history of skin lesions
lesions initially appeared on trunk and spread to upper and proximal lower extremities
lesions were symmetrically distributed and did not coalesce
face, distal extremities, and mucous membranes were unaffected
some lesions resolved spontaneously with residual hyperpigmentation
hypereosinophilia (4220/μL)
elevated tryptase (33.7 ng/mL)
elevated vitamin B12 (>6000 pg/mL)
negative serologic tests for HIV, hepatitis A, B, and C
negative tests for parasitic infections
skin biopsy showed nodular infiltration of histiocytes with lymphocytes and eosinophils
bone marrow analysis showed hypercellularity with myeloid hyperplasia and increased eosinophils

shortlist.label: Erdheim-Chester disease
shortlist.why_kept: characterized by histiocytic infiltration and often presents with skin lesions, bone pain, and elevated tryptase levels

shortlist.label: Langerhans cell histiocytosis
shortlist.why_kept: can present with skin lesions, hypereosinophilia, and elevated vitamin B12 levels

shortlist.label: Indeterminate cell histiocytosis
shortlist.why_kept: a type of histiocytosis that can present with skin lesions and has been associated with hypereosinophilia

shortlist.label: Eosinophilic cellulitis
shortlist.why_kept: characterized by eosinophilic infiltration of the skin and can present with hypereosinophilia and elevated tryptase levels

shortlist.label: Mastocytosis
shortlist.why_kept: can present with skin lesions, hypereosinophilia, and elevated tryptase levels, although the presence of the FIP1L1-PDGFRA fusion gene suggests a myeloproliferative disorder

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of skin lesions, hypereosinophilia, elevated tryptase, and elevated vitamin B12, along with the bone marrow analysis showing hypercellularity with myeloid hyperplasia and increased eosinophils, and the presence of the FIP1L1-PDGFRA fusion gene, are all consistent with Mastocytosis, particularly the systemic form of the disease.

rejected.label: Erdheim-Chester disease
rejected.why: The lack of lipid-laden foam cells or multinucleated giant cells in the skin biopsy and the absence of other typical Erdheim-Chester disease features, such as bone pain or exophthalmos, make this diagnosis less likely.

rejected.label: Langerhans cell histiocytosis
rejected.why: The negative CD1a staining in the skin biopsy and the absence of other typical Langerhans cell histiocytosis features, such as lytic bone lesions or diabetes insipidus, make this diagnosis less likely.

rejected.label: Indeterminate cell histiocytosis
rejected.why: The presence of the FIP1L1-PDGFRA fusion gene and the clinical presentation are not typical for Indeterminate cell histiocytosis.

rejected.label: Eosinophilic cellulitis
rejected.why: The presence of systemic symptoms, such as hypereosinophilia and elevated tryptase, and the bone marrow findings are not typical for Eosinophilic cellulitis, which is usually a localized condition.
